title: Impact of Crop Insurance Subsidy Reform on Agricultural Land Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

The dataset is structured for a canonical DID design with a treatment group (farms exposed to the crop insurance subsidy reform) and a control group, observed in pre- and post-reform periods. The key variable `treat_x_post` is the interaction term that captures the causal effect of the reform.

**Key Assumption: Parallel Trends** — In the absence of the reform, treated and control farms would have followed the same trend in log acres planted. This is plausible if the treatment and control groups were on similar trajectories before the reform, and no other differential shocks occurred simultaneously.

**Specification:**
$$y_{it} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{treated}_i + \beta_2 \cdot \text{post}_t + \beta_3 \cdot \text{treated}_i \times \text{post}_t + \varepsilon_{it}$$

The coefficient $\beta_3$ (on `treat_x_post`) is the DID estimator — the causal effect of the subsidy reform on log acres planted.

## 2. R Code

```r
# =============================================================
# DID Analysis: Crop Insurance Subsidy Reform on Land Use
# =============================================================

library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s40_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "obs x", ncol(df), "cols\n")
cat("\nSummary:\n")
print(summary(df))

# Check group sizes
cat("\n=== Group Sizes ===\n")
print(table(Treated = df$treated, Post = df$post))

# Pre-treatment means by group
cat("\n=== Pre-Treatment Means (log acres) ===\n")
pre_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated, data = df[df$post == 0, ], FUN = mean)
print(pre_means)

cat("\n=== Post-Treatment Means (log acres) ===\n")
post_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated, data = df[df$post == 1, ], FUN = mean)
print(post_means)

# Manual DID calculation
did_manual <- (post_means$y[post_means$treated == 1] - pre_means$y[pre_means$treated == 1]) -
              (post_means$y[post_means$treated == 0] - pre_means$y[pre_means$treated == 0])
cat("\nManual DID estimate:", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")

# =============================================================
# Main DID Regression
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Main DID Regression ===\n")
model_main <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(model_main)

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== DID with Robust Standard Errors (HC1) ===\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(model_main, vcov = vcovHC(model_main, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# Extract key result
beta_did <- coef(model_main)["treat_x_post"]
ci <- confint(model_main, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("DID Estimate (treat_x_post):", round(beta_did, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(ci[1], 4), ",", round(ci[2], 4), "]\n")
cat("p-value:", round(summary(model_main)$coefficients["treat_x_post", 4], 6), "\n")
cat("Interpretation: The reform", ifelse(beta_did > 0, "increased", "decreased"),
    "log acres planted by", round(abs(beta_did), 4), "\n")
cat("  (~", round((exp(beta_did) - 1) * 100, 2), "% change in acres planted)\n")
cat("============================================\n")

# =============================================================
# Robustness Check 1: Clustered SEs by unit
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Clustered SEs by Unit ===\n")
cluster_vcov <- vcovCL(model_main, cluster = df$unit_id)
cluster_test <- coeftest(model_main, vcov = cluster_vcov)
print(cluster_test)

# =============================================================
# Robustness Check 2: Check parallel trends visually with means
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Group Means by Period ===\n")
group_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + period, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(group_means)

# =============================================================
# Robustness Check 3: Wilcoxon rank-sum on DID residuals
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Permutation-style check ===\n")
# Compare treated vs control changes
pre <- df[df$post == 0, c("unit_id", "treated", "y")]
post_df <- df[df$post == 1, c("unit_id", "y")]
if (nrow(pre) == nrow(post_df)) {
  merged <- merge(pre, post_df, by = "unit_id", suffixes = c("_pre", "_post"))
  merged$dy <- merged$y_post - merged$y_pre
  wt <- wilcox.test(dy ~ treated, data = merged)
  cat("Wilcoxon test p-value for differential change:", round(wt$p.value, 4), "\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Positive.** More favorable crop insurance terms reduce downside risk for farmers, making it rational to expand planted acreage (moral hazard / extensive margin response). This is well-documented in the agricultural economics literature (e.g., Goodwin et al., 2004; Yu et al., 2018).

**Expected magnitude:** The DID coefficient ($\beta_3$) is likely positive and in the range of **0.15–0.50 in log points** (roughly 16%–65% increase in acres planted), depending on the generosity of the reform. Given that the outcome is log acres, even a coefficient around 0.3 would imply a ~35% increase, which is plausible for a substantial subsidy reform in a simulated setting. The effect should be statistically significant given the clean experimental-style setup with 150 observations. Robustness checks with heteroskedasticity-robust and clustered standard errors should confirm the baseline finding.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log acres planted between treated and untreated farms before and after the subsidy reform.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The subsidy reform led to an increase in the log of acres planted.
